status: PT-MASTERY data, composed by PT-TUNE (docs/03-tech/pt-tune-design.md): the closing arena of the late-Floor-1 playtest slice. It reuses ONLY the cf02_microarena geometry (floor 580, left perch 544..672, parapet 736..768, right perch 896..992, rotten shore at strike 384, set by the fixture) and the CF02-F wave contract (two waves, checkpoints 128 and 704, no unseen instant damage, the exit opens when the roster is clear). Wave W1 is the brawl lane: a slime with its acid pool in pocket a (176..352), a llama behind the pool and two goblins; it walls off wave W2 behind the parapet. Wave W2 is the llama yard: two goblins in the matador lane, a llama at its home, the Goblin Engineer, and a Rot Sticker under the right perch (pocket b, optional, HAZ rule 10). The sidecar opts in to the wave roster rule (waves: true, PTM-AD6): eight entries in two beats of four, the slime counted in W1. PTM-Q1 landed as ruling (c) in PT-TUNE (PTT-Q7): in a wave room HAZ rule 5 no longer requires every enemy to spawn in a pocket; instead no non-slime enemy body may overlap a pocket or a sticker blast sweep. The existing kinds (goblin, Engineer, llama) stand at their column from tick 0 and wake by sight, so trigger_x and delay_ticks are authoring order only; the delays are distinct because the validator forbids synchronised spawns. Greybox hypotheses, every number a tuning knob: difficulty comes from composition, not HP (#178). The Juicer is not part of this arena. Coordinates are layout pixels, y down, like the room file.
